questions.question: Constraint $i$ of a maximization LP has shadow price $y_i^*$ and RHS sensitivity range $[L,U]$ for $b_i$. How good is the prediction $z^*(b_i^{\mathrm{new}})=z^*(b_i)+y_i^*(b_i^{\mathrm{new}}-b_i)$?
options: Approximate inside $[L,U]$, exact only at $b_i$.
Exact for every $b_i^{\mathrm{new}}$, inside or not.
Exact inside $[L,U]$; outside, it need not hold.
Exact inside $[L,U]$, and an equality outside too.

questions.question: As the right-hand side $b_i$ of a binding constraint in an LP moves towards an endpoint of its RHS sensitivity range, the optimal corner slides along the binding constraints. What happens at the endpoint?
options: Another constraint starts to bind, ending the basis.
The constraint $i$ stops binding and gets positive slack.
The optimal value reaches its largest possible level.
The shadow price of constraint $i$ becomes 0 there.

questions.question: Within its valid range, one kind of parameter change can preserve the optimal solution vector while changing profit, and another can change the solution vector while keeping the same basis and shadow prices. Which change is the second kind?
options: A change in one objective coefficient
A change in two coefficients at once
A change that leaves all data the same
A change in a resource right-hand side

questions.question: In an optimal solution of an LP, a resource constraint has slack 30 and shadow price 0. The right-hand side is cut by 40 units. Is the effect on the optimal value given by $0\cdot(-40)=0$?
options: Yes: a shadow price of 0 holds for any cut.
Yes: a slack resource never affects the plan.
No: the cut goes 10 units past the unused 30.
No: the effect is $-40$, one per unit cut.

questions.question: A binding resource of a maximization LP has its right-hand side changed within its RHS sensitivity range. Which of these stays the same?
options: The basis and all shadow prices
The values of the basic variables
The optimal objective value
The slack of every constraint
